key_insight: Medical multimodal LLMs can be highly confident yet wrong, and this paper shows calibration can be substantially improved with a fusion-based interrogation method plus expert LLM assessment.
clinical_relevance: Better confidence calibration in Medical VQA could make AI-assisted diagnosis more trustworthy by helping users distinguish reliable answers from potentially misleading ones.
method: Multi-Strategy Fusion-Based Interrogation (MS-FBI) to probe model confidence from multiple angles
Auxiliary expert LLM assessment to refine confidence estimates
Evaluate calibration against answer accuracy in medical VQA settings
evidence_signal: Across three Medical VQA datasets, the proposed approach reduced Expected Calibration Error (ECE) by an average of 40% and improved alignment between confidence and correctness.
watch_item: Calibration gains in Medical VQA may not generalize to other clinical tasks or real-world workflows without further validation and safety testing.
paper_title: Confidence Calibration for Multimodal LLMs: An Empirical Study through Medical VQA
